name: HomeVisioner: AI Room Visualizer
author: HomeVisioner

sections.description:
HomeVisioner: AI Room Visualizer shows a shopper what a rug, a piece of furniture or a wall or floor covering looks like in their own room. The shopper uploads a photo of the room on your product page, and HomeVisioner returns an AI-generated picture of that room with your product in it.

What you get:

  • A “See it in your room” button on single product pages. The button and the window it opens are the HomeVisioner service’s storefront widget, loaded from the service like any hosted widget. On variable products the visualization follows the variation the shopper has chosen. The window shows a small “Powered by HomeVisioner” link at its foot, part of the service’s widget; on the Pro plan it can be turned off in the HomeVisioner panel. The plugin adds no credit or link anywhere else on your site.
  • AI room visualization of your own product photos in the shopper’s room photo.
  • Add to cart from the result. Next to the picture of their room, the shopper can add the product, with the chosen variation, to your WooCommerce cart.
  • A HomeVisioner page in WordPress admin, under WooCommerce → HomeVisioner: your plan, this month’s usage and the last 30 days at a glance, and an Open HomeVisioner button. The button opens the HomeVisioner panel (dashboard, products, customers, analytics, gallery, settings and billing) in a new browser tab on panel.homevisioner.com, already signed in from WordPress: there is no separate HomeVisioner login or password.
  • Shopper email collection. After a few free previews the shopper is asked for an email address to keep going, with a separate, optional checkbox for marketing emails. You see the collected contacts in the HomeVisioner panel.
  • Order analytics. HomeVisioner reads your orders (read-only) to show how many orders came from shoppers who used the visualizer, matched by email address.
  • Emails. HomeVisioner emails you about your account: a welcome, usage nearing or reaching your plan’s limit, plan changes and a monthly summary. You choose which ones in the settings. A shopper who could not get a preview because your limit was reached, and asked to be told, gets one email when previews work again.

The plugin itself is small: it connects your store, prints the button script and the product it belongs to on product pages, and adds the HomeVisioner page to WP admin, from which the HomeVisioner panel opens. It does not change your theme files, your products or your orders.

This plugin needs a HomeVisioner account, which is created for your store when you connect. It is compatible with WooCommerce’s High-Performance Order Storage (HPOS).

Plans

There is a Free plan, and paid Starter, Growth and Pro plans with more visualizations per month; they are the same plans HomeVisioner offers on Shopify. Paid plans are billed monthly by card through Stripe (there is no yearly plan), and are chosen, changed and cancelled on the Billing page of the HomeVisioner panel (WooCommerce → HomeVisioner → Billing). Plans and current prices: https://www.homevisioner.com/woocommerce

Try it

A WooCommerce demo store with HomeVisioner installed: https://demo.homevisioner.com

External services

This plugin connects to the HomeVisioner service at https://panel.homevisioner.com, operated by HomeVisioner (https://www.homevisioner.com). Without it the plugin does nothing: the visualization, the HomeVisioner panel and the analytics all run there.

What is sent, and when:

  • When you click “Connect store”: your browser is sent to the HomeVisioner service with your store’s address (the WordPress home URL), the address of this plugin’s page to return to, and a one-time code. Nothing is sent before you click. WooCommerce then shows you its own consent screen, and if you approve, WooCommerce sends HomeVisioner a read-only REST API key for your store. When you return, the plugin sends the one-time code, your store address, the plugin version and your site language (used for the emails HomeVisioner sends you) to the service, and receives this store’s connection details.
  • While connected, from the HomeVisioner service to your store: using that read-only key, the service reads your products (names, images, variations and categories), your store currency and your orders (including the order’s billing email address, used only to match orders to shoppers who used the visualizer). It never writes to your store.
  • On product pages, from your shoppers’ browsers, while connected: the button script (https://panel.homevisioner.com/storefront/woocommerce/widget.js), its stylesheet and images are loaded from the HomeVisioner service on every single product page. When the page opens, the script asks the service whether the button is switched on for this product (sending the product id) and sends usage counts the HomeVisioner panel shows as analytics: that the product page was viewed and that the button was seen, with the product and variation id and a random visitor id. That id is kept in the shopper’s browser (localStorage, no cookie) so that repeat views and the shopper’s earlier previews can be recognised; it is not linked to any other site. When a shopper uses the button, the button being opened, the room photo the shopper uploads, the chosen variation, the shopper’s email address if they enter one, add-to-cart from the result and any feedback on the result are sent to the HomeVisioner service. Room photos are processed by HomeVisioner’s AI image providers to create the visualization. Add to cart itself goes to your own store, not to HomeVisioner.
  • When you open WooCommerce → HomeVisioner while connected: your WordPress server asks the service for a short summary (GET https://panel.homevisioner.com/plugin/summary/woocommerce), sending your store address, the current time and a signature made with your store’s connection secret. The service answers with your plan, this period’s usage and the number of visualizations and collected shopper emails in the last 30 days, which the page shows. The answer is kept for five minutes. Nothing is requested while the page is not open.
  • When you click “Open HomeVisioner” or one of the links beside it: your browser is sent, in a new tab, to the HomeVisioner panel at https://panel.homevisioner.com, with your store address, the current time, the panel page you chose and a signature made with your store’s connection secret. The link works for two minutes; the panel session it starts lasts one hour, after which you open the panel again from WooCommerce → HomeVisioner.
  • When you disconnect, deactivate or delete the plugin, while connected: a signed notice with your store address, the time and the plugin version (on deactivation) or the reason (disconnect or deletion) is sent to the service so it can mark your store disconnected. If the store was never connected, nothing is sent.
  • Emails: HomeVisioner sends account emails to the contact address you enter in the HomeVisioner panel, and one notification email to a shopper who asked to be told when previews work again.

HomeVisioner’s terms of service: https://www.homevisioner.com/agb
HomeVisioner’s privacy policy: https://www.homevisioner.com/privacy
HomeVisioner’s data processing addendum: https://www.homevisioner.com/dpa

When a shopper uploads a room photo, the button script first checks, inside the shopper’s browser, that the photo shows a room and not a person. For this it loads Google’s MediaPipe face detector: the code from the jsDelivr CDN (https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@mediapipe/tasks-vision@1.0.1/) and the detection model from Google Cloud Storage (https://storage.googleapis.com/mediapipe-models/). Only these files are downloaded; the photo is not sent to jsDelivr or Google, and the check runs on the shopper’s device. Like any download, it reveals the shopper’s IP address and browser to those hosts. jsDelivr’s terms: https://www.jsdelivr.com/terms, privacy policy: https://www.jsdelivr.com/terms/privacy-policy-jsdelivr-net. Google’s terms: https://policies.google.com/terms, privacy policy: https://policies.google.com/privacy

The HomeVisioner panel uses two further services. The plugin itself does not contact them; the panel does, in its own tab:

  • Stripe (https://stripe.com), for paid plans. When you choose a paid plan or manage billing on the panel’s Billing page, you are sent to Stripe’s checkout or billing portal, and your card details are entered there; HomeVisioner never sees them. Stripe’s services agreement: https://stripe.com/legal/ssa, privacy policy: https://stripe.com/privacy
  • Crisp (https://crisp.chat), the support chat in the HomeVisioner panel. Its script is loaded when the panel opens, with your store’s name and HomeVisioner plan so support knows who is writing; what you type in the chat is sent to Crisp. Crisp’s terms: https://crisp.chat/en/terms/, privacy policy: https://crisp.chat/en/privacy/

You are responsible for telling your shoppers about this processing in your own store’s privacy policy.
sections.installation:
1. Make sure WooCommerce 8.0 or newer is installed and active, and that your store is served over HTTPS.
  2. Upload the plugin through Plugins → Add New → Upload Plugin, or install it from the WordPress plugin directory, and activate it.
  3. Go to WooCommerce → HomeVisioner and click Connect store.
  4. Approve read-only access on WooCommerce’s consent screen. You are brought back to WooCommerce → HomeVisioner, which now shows your store as connected.
  5. Click Open HomeVisioner. The panel opens in a new tab; check its Products and Settings pages, which decide on which product pages the button appears and how it looks.
sections.faq:
Does it change my theme?

No. The plugin edits no theme files and adds no templates. On single product pages it adds the HomeVisioner script and a small, invisible block of product data (id, name, main image, price, stock, variations and the cart addresses the add-to-cart button uses) through WordPress’s standard hooks. Deactivating the plugin removes both.

What access does HomeVisioner get to my store?

A read-only WooCommerce REST API key, created through WooCommerce’s own consent screen. You can see it under WooCommerce → Settings → Advanced → REST API. HomeVisioner can read products and orders with it; it cannot change anything.

Why does it need HTTPS?

WooCommerce only hands out REST API keys safely over HTTPS, so connecting is refused on a store served over plain HTTP.

How do I disconnect?

Go to WooCommerce → HomeVisioner and click Disconnect at the bottom of the page. The plugin tells the HomeVisioner service, revokes the REST API key it was given, and forgets the connection. The button disappears from your product pages. You can connect again at any time.

Deactivating the plugin only hides the button; the connection is kept, so reactivating needs no new connection.

What is deleted when I delete the plugin?

Deleting the plugin from the Plugins screen tells the HomeVisioner service that the store was removed, revokes the HomeVisioner REST API key in WooCommerce, and deletes the plugin’s options (the connection details, the shared secret and any unfinished connection attempt) and its cached summary. The plugin creates no database tables of its own.

Data held by the HomeVisioner service (for example generated images, collected shopper emails and analytics) is handled as described in HomeVisioner’s privacy policy; contact HomeVisioner to have it deleted.

What does it cost?

There is a Free plan, and paid Starter, Growth and Pro plans with higher limits, the same plans as HomeVisioner on Shopify. Paid plans are billed monthly by card through Stripe (there is no yearly plan). Plans are chosen and managed on the Billing page of the HomeVisioner panel, which opens from WooCommerce → HomeVisioner; plans and current prices are on https://www.homevisioner.com/woocommerce.

Can I try it before installing?

Yes. The demo store at https://demo.homevisioner.com runs WooCommerce with HomeVisioner: open a product and click “See it in your room”.

Why does the HomeVisioner panel open in a new tab?

The panel is part of the HomeVisioner service and runs on its own site, panel.homevisioner.com, not inside WordPress. The WooCommerce → HomeVisioner page shows a short summary and opens the panel in its own tab, signed in through a one-time link from WordPress. If the tab stays open for more than an hour, the panel asks you to open it again from WooCommerce → HomeVisioner.

Which languages does it support?

The plugin’s own admin texts are written in English; translations come from translate.wordpress.org in your site language. The HomeVisioner panel follows your site language in 18 languages: Chinese (Simplified and Traditional), Czech, Danish, Dutch, English, Finnish, French, German, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Norwegian, Polish, Portuguese (Brazil), Spanish, Swedish and Turkish. The shopper-facing button and window follow your storefront’s language in 22 languages: Arabic, Bulgarian, Chinese (Simplified and Traditional), Czech, Danish, Dutch, English, Finnish, French, German, Hebrew, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Norwegian, Polish, Portuguese (Brazil), Romanian, Spanish, Swedish and Turkish.
sections.changelog:
0.1.1

  • WooCommerce → HomeVisioner is now a summary page (plan, usage, last 30 days) with an Open HomeVisioner button. The HomeVisioner panel opens in a new tab on panel.homevisioner.com, signed in through a one-time link from WordPress, instead of inside a frame in WP admin.
  • Quick links open the panel’s Products, Settings, Analytics and Billing pages directly.
  • Translations are no longer bundled with the plugin; WordPress loads them from translate.wordpress.org.

0.1.0

  • First release: connect the store with a read-only WooCommerce REST API key, the “See it in your room” button on single product pages (including variable products) with add to cart from the result, the HomeVisioner screens in WooCommerce → HomeVisioner, disconnect and uninstall clean-up, Turkish translation.

short_description: Let shoppers see your products in their own room. Adds a "See it in your room" button to product pages and a HomeVisioner page to WooCommerce.

screenshots.caption: Shoppers upload a photo of their room and see your product in it, then add it to cart from the result.
One visualizer for every category: rugs, furniture, flooring and home décor, from your existing product images.
Mobile-friendly room previews in three steps: upload, generate, preview and buy.
Setup: install the plugin, connect your store in WooCommerce → HomeVisioner, then open the HomeVisioner panel and style the button to match your brand with a live preview.
Choose where the widget appears, by category or by product.
Capture customer leads: shoppers leave their email in the visualizer, and you see them in the HomeVisioner panel.
Track visualizations, leads, orders and revenue in the HomeVisioner panel; WooCommerce → HomeVisioner shows your plan, usage and the last 30 days at a glance.
